> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e7a82a61bb550a291fe1b99f939f7472be2166ff` — the merge of head `d50adfbfd254e8c187c2b67c7d16d53e57fbb6a8` into base `2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e7a82a61bb550a291fe1b99f939f7472be2166ff && git checkout e7a82a61bb550a291fe1b99f939f7472be2166ff
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0 d50adfbfd254e8c187c2b67c7d16d53e57fbb6a8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0 && git merge --no-ff d50adfbfd254e8c187c2b67c7d16d53e57fbb6a8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2f80f2897a4c484c9ff445d268ab83e1ce16a6d0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Nothing was built or run; every finding below is from reading the tree, and F1 says so again because its grade rests on it.

**Result: PASS with one should-fix (F1) and three nits (F2 to F4).** The fix does what the card and the epic ruling ask on a host with no declared package. F1 is one answer that moves without a FROM → TO row or a pin, on a host whose declared package is one of the two holders.

Check-runs on this head at this reading: 0 failed. Completed and green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, the three scoped lints, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI. Still running: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, · consumer gates, · debt ledger, and Lint · CI, release and engine gates. This PASS does not stand in for those; a red one among them overrides it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Bare `get` / `getDiagnosed` after the boot pass, two holders: served body → `409 ambiguous-in-environment` naming both.** Right. It is the epic ruling carried on the claim, and the same read without the pass already refused. Narrowing, first-party 0: no package, app or example calls `setDatabaseDriver`, `setDataEngine` or passes `config.driver` (grep at this head).
- **Runtime bare `/actions` door and MCP `run_action` with no merged listing: ran → `409`.** Right. The door's code is untouched; its input (`loadMany('action')`) now carries both declarations. Pinned at the door over a real manager and loader.
- **`DatabaseLoader.loadMany` / `loadManyKeyed`: one row per name → one per `(package, name)` for a contested name only.** Right, and the code matches: `unscopedTypeRows` switches key only where `namesSeveralPackagesHold` names the row's name. A legacy row keys into its own package's slot, so it is an older row of that slot and not a third holder.
- **`MetadataManager.loadMany` / `loadManyKeyed`: one per `body.name` → one per store slot for a contested name, earlier loader kept per slot.** Right. Contest is counted over every loader's items after the stamp, so two loaders each holding one package's item also hand on both.
- **Single-holder answers (red line 3): unchanged.** Holds by construction: a package-less item is never counted as a holder, an uncontested name keeps the key `name`, and `primingOrder` cannot reorder a name that hands on one item. C2 to C5 pin it, including the host-package variants.
- **`email_template` (bundled): unchanged.** Holds: `pluralEntryKey` returns `bundleEntryKey` first and `primingOrder` returns bundled types as handed.
- **Not declared: a read naming the host's own package, two holders and a package-less row.** Wrong as it stands; see F1.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch` with the `!` title, the BREAKING paragraph and an ADR-0087 `not-required` disposition. This matches the rule for a non-protocol change (`Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` and keeps its banner). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is on both the PR body and the changeset, and the two texts agree. No runtime changeset is owed: the runtime diff is test-only. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Deviation, two narrowing arms: accepted; both are declared with FROM → TO and pinned (rows 1 and 8).
- Deviation, content pairing added to `withLoaderEntryPackages`: accepted as the way to keep #32458's F3 rule; see F3 and F4 for its limits.
- Deviation, runtime test file: accepted; the ruling asks for the moved answer pinned where it is answered.
- Deviation, dogfood battery ran one `main` merge before this head: not judged here; the head's own check-runs are the gate and the Test Core shards are still running.
- Out-of-scope finding, package-less action row filed as one holder's customization of an object: agreed that this PR does not move it. It is not filed anywhere ("noted, not filed"); it should get a card so it is not lost.
- `security_findings: withheld` in the dev report: not visible to this review. Nothing security-relevant was found in the four files.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the spec on `main`: it makes the store's own refusal (`readStoreEntry`, D3) reachable after a boot. It takes no declared capability away.

**F1 — should-fix. On a host whose declared package is one of the two holders, a package-less row of the name replaces that holder's own item in the registry, and the answer of a read naming that package moves with no row and no pin.**
Shape: rows ALPHA, BETA and a package-less row of `helper`; `MetadataPlugin` constructed with `packageId: ALPHA`.
- `primingOrder` registers ALPHA's and BETA's items first, then the package-less one. `applyProtection` stamps that one with the host's package (it carries no `_packageId`), so `storeWriteKey` files it into ALPHA's slot and overwrites ALPHA's own item.
- TO: `get(type, 'helper', ALPHA)` answers the package-less body, in every save order. Without the pass it answers ALPHA's own body.
- FROM: ALPHA's own body, read through the loaders, whenever the package-less row was not the one saved last (two of three orders); the package-less body when it was.
- The bare read is still refused naming both, so red line 2 holds in this shape.
- Three sentences are untrue here: `primingOrder`'s jsdoc ("under a name two packages hold, the name's bare slot"; "the registry holds what a read without the pass answers, whatever order"), and PR row 7 ("a read naming a package its own item … all as without the pass"). The row-7 pins call `bootPass()` with no host package, so nothing covers it.
- This was read, not run. First step for the dev: measure it. If the answer does not move, this finding is withdrawn.
- Fix, either one: declare the row FROM → TO with its arm and pin it, if the epic seat rules that the host's stamp makes that row the host's item (the one-holder CONTROL already behaves this way); or keep a contested name's package-less item out of the host stamp so it stays in the bare slot as the jsdoc says. Reach is first-party 0. It is graded should-fix and not nit because an undeclared moved answer is the epic's own red-line clause.
- Related, no separate grade: with a host package that is neither holder, the package-less row lands in the host's slot and the bare refusal names three packages, not two.

**F2 — nit, follow-up card. In #32458's F3 shape the bare read after the pass still answers one body.** Two holders plus another row whose body says the name: nothing is stamped, the manager sees no contest, and one unstamped body is registered in the bare slot. The guess moves from BETA's body to ALPHA's (row 6b, declared, pinned at `loadMany`). The red-line-2 breach in this shape predates the PR and is not widened by it, but the card's "two holders → bare read 409" is not met there. It needs its own card; the epic seat may regrade it.

**F3 — nit, follow-up card. Content pairing is a workaround for `loadMany` carrying no row key.** `withLoaderEntryPackages` pairs a body to its keyed entry by `JSON.stringify` equality. For `DatabaseLoader` both reads come from the same rows, so it holds. A loader whose `loadMany` and `loadManyKeyed` bodies serialise differently is left unstamped with no signal and falls back to one item per name. Reading a contested name's bodies from the keyed entries directly (as the bundled path does) would remove this, and probably F2 as well (not checked).

**F4 — nit, follow-up card. `MetadataManager.loadManyKeyed` drops `packageId` from the entries it returns.** For a contested name bound by the column only it now returns two entries with the same `name` and unstamped `data`, so a caller cannot tell the holders apart and a caller keying by name collapses them (row 10's audit counts two but cannot name them). The loader's entries carry `packageId`; the manager's `{ name, data }` discards it.

Sentence-by-sentence agreement otherwise: `namesSeveralPackagesHold`, `pluralEntryKey`, the `unscopedTypeRows` jsdoc, the `admitKeyedLoaderEntries` jsdoc and the changeset bullets match the code. The no-`loadManyKeyed` fallback now loads every listed name of a slotted type; all three first-party loaders implement the keyed read, so it is reachable only from a third-party loader.

Delta review owed on F1's fix. F2 to F4 go to follow-up cards, not another round.
